nodes.description: The OAuth1/OAuth2 credential authorization flow must be able to generate the authorization URL and handle the callback.
The webhook, webhook-test, webhook-waiting, form, form-test, and form-waiting root routes must exist.
The task broker must expose the runners websocket and the broker auth surface.
The scope catalog must cover at least high-frequency domains such as workflows, credentials, projects, variables, users, tags, AI, and MCP.
The setup and reset commands must be provided in package.json or an equivalent command entry point.
The dev:web, dev:worker, dev:webhook, dev:frontend, dev:e2e, and dev:gateway commands must be provided in package.json or an equivalent command entry point.
The build and build:docker commands must be provided in package.json or an equivalent command entry point.
The test, test:unit, test:integration, test:e2e, and test:db-compat commands must be provided in package.json or an equivalent command entry point.
The lint, format, typecheck, report:licenses, and report:test commands must be provided in package.json or an equivalent command entry point.
The frontend must retain a unified routing entry point and implement the 8 mandatory page views.
The usability of the workflow canvas editor, node details panel, and node drag-and-drop plus connection-wiring interactions needs to be scored by an LLM.

inputs.rubric_prompt: Evaluate whether this Vue 3 + Element Plus frontend provides a workflow canvas editor, a node details panel, and node drag-and-drop plus connection-wiring interactions. Full score = 6 points (canvas + node panel + connection interaction all present and usable), 3 points = a basic canvas exists but interactions are missing, 0 points = no canvas editor.

nodes.description: Multi-page routing capabilities such as project/folder navigation, the AI build and chat workspace, and error/no-permission pages need to be scored by an LLM.

inputs.rubric_prompt: Evaluate whether this frontend provides multi-page routing capabilities such as a project/folder navigation sidebar, an AI build and chat workspace, an OAuth consent page, an error page, and a no-permission page. Full score = 6 points (navigation + AI workspace + error handling all present), 3 points = navigation exists but the AI or error pages are missing, 0 points = the navigation structure is missing.

nodes.description: The visual hierarchy and responsive handling of high-density pages such as workflows, projects, and credentials under desktop and mobile layouts need to be scored by an LLM.

inputs.rubric_prompt: Evaluate whether this frontend is clear and consistent in its visual hierarchy, information-density control, responsive layout, and Element Plus component composition across list pages, detail pages, edit pages, and the side navigation. If it is merely a stack of bare tables, lacks a layout strategy on mobile, or has a chaotic information hierarchy, it should be given a low score.

nodes.description: The comprehensibility of login, OAuth consent, error pages, empty states, and no-permission feedback needs to be scored by an LLM.

inputs.rubric_prompt: Evaluate whether the frontend provides clear feedback for states such as login, OAuth consent, empty lists, 404/500, permission denial, and long-task waiting, rather than only showing the browser's default error or a blank page. If boundary states are missing or the copy is completely incomprehensible, it should be given a low score.

nodes.description: The backend needs to be cleanly layered into an Express routing layer, domain services, a TypeORM persistence layer, and a Bull/Redis asynchronous layer, rather than piling workflows, AI, chat, and permissions all into a single module.

inputs.rubric_prompt: Evaluate whether the backend clearly separates modules such as authentication/authorization, projects and sharing, workflow execution, data tables, chat and AI, and Webhook/task queues, and adopts clear boundaries such as Express routes/controllers, domain services, TypeORM entities and migrations, and Bull workers. If all logic is crammed into a single entry file or a single service, it should be given a low score.

nodes.description: The modeling boundaries of projects, shared resources, role permissions, and public API keys need to be scored by an LLM.

inputs.rubric_prompt: Evaluate whether the backend cleanly layers session authentication, public API keys, project sharing, the role matrix, and resource-ownership relationships, rather than scattering permission checks across large amounts of duplicated if/else. If the shared-resource and permission models are chaotic and lack a centralized strategy, it should be given a low score.

nodes.description: The contract-organization quality of REST, the public API, Webhook/Form, MCP/OAuth, and long-connection entry points needs to be scored by an LLM.

inputs.rubric_prompt: Evaluate whether the backend uses clear routing, DTO/validation, error wrapping, and serialization strategies for the different interface surfaces such as /rest, /api/v1, Webhook/Form, OAuth/MCP, and SSE/WebSocket. If all entry points are mixed into the same layer and envelope handling is chaotic, it should be given a low score.
